sentences.text: The only known species, Elmisaurus rarus, lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia, though other estimates suggest a range from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
The generic name means "foot sole" because the type specimen consisted of a metatarsus.
Two fragmentary specimens of a small theropod were discovered in 1970 by a Polish-Mongolian expedition in the Ömnögovĭ province of Mongolia.
A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and colleagues examined 23 foot bones referred to Elmisaurus for stress fractures but found none.
A 2013 analysis by Longrich et al. classified Elmisaurus as a caenagnathid.
Elmisaurus lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
In 1997, Hans-Dieter Sues argued that the second species should be referred to Chirostenotes, a view not accepted by Philip J. Currie.
